objective.statement: Know the Italian, German and French terms and directions of Grade 5 and use them.
successCriteria: I know the Italian terms of Grade 5.
I can translate simple German and French directions such as sehr langsam or très lent.
I know the piano pedal and hand directions.

explanation.text: Grade 5 adds more Italian terms: for example attacca (go straight on to the next section), dolente (sad, mournful), doppio movimento (twice as fast), estinto (as soft as possible), incalzando (getting quicker), lusingando (coaxing), ossia (or, alternatively), piangevole (plaintive), rinforzando (reinforcing), smorzando (dying away), teneramente (tenderly), tosto (swift) and volante (flying, fast).

German directions are built from short words: langsam (slow), schnell (fast), lebhaft (lively), ruhig (peaceful), bewegt (with movement), zart (tender), breit (broad), traurig (sad), süss (sweet), fröhlich (cheerful), mässig (at a moderate speed). Little words change them: sehr (very), etwas (somewhat), wenig (little), nicht (not), zu (too), immer (always), wieder (again), und (and), mit (with), ohne (without), aber (but). Sehr langsam is 'very slow'; mit Ausdruck is 'with expression'. French directions work in the same way: lent (slow), vif (lively), vite (quick), léger (light), douce (sweet, gentle), modéré (at a moderate speed), animé (animated), with little words such as très (very), assez (enough), peu (little), plus (more), moins (less), sans (without), avec (with), mais (but), et (and); cédez, ralentir and retenu all ask for a slower speed, and avec sourdines means 'with mutes'. Très lent is 'very slow'.

music.textAlternative: Four crotchets marked etwas lebhaft, somewhat lively.

explanation.caption: Etwas lebhaft: ‘somewhat lively’. A direction like this is printed above the first bar.

explanation.text: Pianists also meet directions for the pedals and hands: una corda (press the left pedal, literally 'one string'), tre corde (release the left pedal, 'three strings'), mano sinistra (m.s., left hand) and mano destra (m.d., right hand).

Learn a term with its meaning in a short phrase, and notice words you already know. Terms with similar meanings (for example dolente and piangevole) are never offered as wrong answers for each other, so the right answer is always the only one that fits.
German: translate word by word. Italian: link the term to its mood or action.

provenance.notes: Original meanings. The term list is the one in First Steps Grade 5 section 15 (pp. 140-142, read in the PDF) plus the French list printed on p. 104, which the Grade 5 practice papers test (GRADE_5_PAPER_COMPARISON P1); the official outline gives no list so a teacher must confirm it (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q2). Grade 4 terms are never asked here.
